status: frozen mechanism and inferred shared management range before simulation; unaccepted
source_family: al-Nabulusi cadastral survey, modern scholarly edition and spatial reconstruction; related evidence

sources.role: canal system and local water allocation

license: No open redistribution license established for cached project pages; source links and derived findings only in handoff
mechanism: Gravity-fed branch and feeder canals, weirs and village water allocations support maintained agriculture in the Fayyum depression. This is not conditional on a native game river flag.
spatial_basis: Named Faiyum game location at calibrated 29.328 N, 30.806 E; no population-derived selector or area allocation

assessment.numerical_basis: Reuse the existing maintained Egyptian hydraulic-system game range. Numbers are inferred management and operational-coverage bounds, not measurements in the historical survey. Canal and basin techniques remain distinct source mechanisms.

expected_effect: Correct the generic agricultural analogue to maintained canal agriculture; change management effectiveness and incremental water support without adding hectares or future infrastructure
regression_case: Complete Bahnasa province, unchanged/low/central/high at 100 and 200 years with all neighbouring assignments, population composition and food-building output fixed
exclusions: No new cultivated hectares or allocation of the Upper Egypt 8,400 km2 estimate
No automatic additional annual crop or repeated canal/reservoir benefit
No higher-pop consumption reduction or additional urban food
No equivalence between medieval tribal affiliations and the native tribesmen population class
uncertainty: Continuity from mid-thirteenth-century evidence to 1337 is an inferred pre-plague scenario
The historical lake level differs from the modern one; extent reconstruction remains separate
The map combines historical texts, later surveys, modern elevation and revised canal routes; not every settlement is located
No attained yield estimate is imported, so the existing yield/development normalization remains unchanged
